# CLI Reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_cli_reference.py from the shipped argparse tree. Do not edit by hand; regenerate. -->

HADES ships two programs: `hades`, the command-line tool documented here, and `hades-server`, which starts the REST API server directly. `hades serve` starts the same API application from the main program, with the options listed below. Every command and option below is read from the parser the binary uses. Run `hades <command> --help` for the same information on your installed version.

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`hades scan`](#hades-scan) | Scan files and directories for metadata threats |
| [`hades forensics`](#hades-forensics) | Extract and display metadata forensics for a file |
| [`hades monitor`](#hades-monitor) | Watch directories and auto-scan new/modified files |
| [`hades case`](#hades-case) | Evidence chain and case management |
| [`hades serve`](#hades-serve) | Start the HADES REST API server |
| [`hades benchmark`](#hades-benchmark) | Run performance benchmarks |
| [`hades plugin`](#hades-plugin) | Manage detection plugins |
| [`hades intel`](#hades-intel) | Threat intelligence and ML detection management |
| [`hades rules`](#hades-rules) | YARA rule management |
| [`hades admin`](#hades-admin) | User, license, tenant, and system administration |
| [`hades doctor`](#hades-doctor) | Check system health and dependency status |
| [`hades sanitize`](#hades-sanitize) | Remove metadata from a file or directory |
| [`hades update`](#hades-update) | Check for and install HADES updates |
| [`hades licenses`](#hades-licenses) | Show third-party attribution and bundled license texts |
| [`hades feedback`](#hades-feedback) | Report a false positive to DarkHorse, or check a report's status |

## `hades scan`

Scan files or directories for hidden metadata threats, malformed payloads, and suspicious patterns.

```
hades scan [-h] [-r] [--file-types FILE_TYPES] [--exclude-types EXCLUDE_TYPES] [--all-files] [--fail-on {critical,high,medium,low,never}] [--archives] [--max-file-size MAX_FILE_SIZE] [--workers WORKERS] [--timeout TIMEOUT] [--yara-rules DIR_OR_FILE] [--ti-feeds CONFIG_FILE] [--allowlist FILE] [--config FILE] [--min-score MIN_SCORE] [--max-score MAX_SCORE] [--sort-by {score,name,size,time}] [--sort-order {asc,desc}] [--filter-level {safe,low,medium,high,critical}] [--limit LIMIT] [-o FILE] [--format {json,csv,text,html,pdf}] [--template FILE] [--include-metadata] [--executive-summary] [--audit-mode] [--chain-custody] [--compliance-mode {gdpr,hipaa,sox}] [--encrypt-output] [--case-id ID] [--ir-mode] [-v] [-q] [--debug] [--log-file FILE] [--performance-metrics] [--async] [--concurrency CONCURRENCY] [--cache] [--no-cache] [--profile] [--firmware-scan] [--firmware-allowlist PATH] [--firmware-ml] [--ml-detect] [--behavioral] [--mitre-map] [--deep-format] [--forensics] [--threat-intel] [--ti-providers {virustotal,abuseipdb,otx,malwarebazaar} [{virustotal,abuseipdb,otx,malwarebazaar} ...]] [--ti-offline] [--siem-format {cef,syslog,stix,leef,ecs}] [--siem-output {file,syslog,http,stdout}] [--siem-target TARGET] [--siem-min-severity SCORE] [--analytics] [--analytics-period PERIOD] [--analytics-export FILE] [--plugins-dir PLUGINS_DIR] [--disable-plugins] paths [paths ...]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `paths` | Files or directories to analyze |  |
| `-r, --recursive` | Recursively process directories |  |
| `--file-types FILE_TYPES` | File extensions to process, comma-separated (e.g., --file-types .jpg,.pdf,.exe). The v1.4.4 space-separated form (--file-types .jpg .pdf) is deprecated and will emit a warning. |  |
| `--exclude-types EXCLUDE_TYPES` | File extensions to exclude, comma-separated |  |
| `--all-files` | Scan every file found, ignoring the default extension allowlist (useful for .dat/.bin/.tmp/.img corpora). --exclude-types still applies. |  |
| `--fail-on {critical,high,medium,low,never}` | Exit code policy (default: high). Exit 1 when any file is at or above this level; 'never' always exits 0 for findings. Exit codes: 0 = every file scanned and none at or above the level; 1 = findings at or above the level; 2 = usage or tool error; 3 = no findings at the level but some files were NOT SCANNED. | `high` |
| `--archives` | Also scan the files inside .zip and tar archives (.tar, .tar.gz, .tgz, .tar.bz2, .tar.xz), nested up to 3 levels. Members are reported as archive.zip!path/inside. Extraction is bounded (100 MB per file, 1 GB per archive, 4 GB per scan, 10,000 members per archive) and refuses links and unsafe paths; any archive whose contents were not all extracted (7z, encrypted or refused members, limits reached) is reported as NOT SCANNED. The archive files themselves are always scanned. |  |
| `--max-file-size MAX_FILE_SIZE` | Maximum file size to process (e.g., 50MB, 1GB). Default: 100MB | `100MB` |
| `--workers WORKERS` | RESERVED: scanning is currently single-threaded; this value is accepted but does not yet parallelize (see --timeout for the per-file bound). Use scripts/hades_batch.py for parallel corpus runs. | `4` |
| `--timeout TIMEOUT` | Timeout per file in seconds (default: 30). Bounds the wait and moves on; a file that exceeds it is reported with status 'timeout'. | `30` |
| `--yara-rules DIR_OR_FILE` | Custom YARA rules directory or file |  |
| `--ti-feeds CONFIG_FILE` | Threat intelligence feeds configuration file |  |
| `--allowlist FILE` | Allowlist patterns file for false positive reduction |  |
| `--config FILE` | Main configuration file path |  |
| `--min-score MIN_SCORE` | Minimum threat score to report (0-100, default: 0) | `0` |
| `--max-score MAX_SCORE` | Maximum threat score to report (0-100, default: 100) | `100` |
| `--sort-by {score,name,size,time}` | Sort results by field (default: score) | `score` |
| `--sort-order {asc,desc}` | Sort order (default: desc) | `desc` |
| `--filter-level {safe,low,medium,high,critical}` | Filter results by threat level |  |
| `--limit LIMIT` | Limit number of results to display |  |
| `-o FILE, --output FILE` | Output file path |  |
| `--format {json,csv,text,html,pdf}` | Output format (default: text) | `text` |
| `--template FILE` | Custom report template file |  |
| `--include-metadata` | Include detailed metadata in reports |  |
| `--executive-summary` | Generate executive summary section |  |
| `--audit-mode` | Enable comprehensive audit logging |  |
| `--chain-custody` | Include chain of custody information |  |
| `--compliance-mode {gdpr,hipaa,sox}` | Enable specific compliance reporting mode |  |
| `--encrypt-output` | Encrypt sensitive output files |  |
| `--case-id ID` | Associate scans with an existing case ID |  |
| `--ir-mode` | Incident-response mode: disable PII/PHI redaction in every scan output (report, stdout, --siem-format). By default HADES masks emails, phones, SSNs, cards, user-home paths, dates (kept to the year), labelled MRN/patient/member/account IDs, labelled names and addresses, and ZIP codes. Use only on incident-investigation workflows where the analyst needs the raw values. No unredacted copy is kept anywhere else. See docs/pii_redaction.md. |  |
| `-v, --verbose` | Verbose output with detailed progress |  |
| `-q, --quiet` | Quiet mode (minimal output) |  |
| `--debug` | Enable debug mode with detailed logging |  |
| `--log-file FILE` | Log file path |  |
| `--performance-metrics` | Collect and display performance metrics |  |
| `--async` | Use async scan pipeline for improved throughput |  |
| `--concurrency CONCURRENCY` | Number of concurrent scans in async mode (default: 4) | `4` |
| `--cache` | Enable scan result caching |  |
| `--no-cache` | Disable scan result caching |  |
| `--profile` | Enable scan profiling for this session |  |
| `--firmware-scan` | Enable verbose firmware-specific analysis output |  |
| `--firmware-allowlist PATH` | Path to known-good firmware hash allowlist file |  |
| `--firmware-ml` | Enable ML-based firmware anomaly detection (requires scikit-learn) |  |
| `--ml-detect` | Enable ML-based anomaly detection on scans |  |
| `--behavioral` | Enable behavioral/campaign analysis across scanned files |  |
| `--mitre-map` | Show MITRE ATT&CK mapping for scan results |  |
| `--deep-format` | Force deep format analysis (PDF, Office, SVG, polyglot) |  |
| `--forensics` | Attach a metadata-forensics disclosure section (GPS, camera serial, author, edit history, thumbnail crop-delta) to each result. Additive and informational -- never changes the malware verdict. Professional+. |  |
| `--threat-intel` | Enable cloud threat intelligence enrichment on scans |  |
| `--ti-providers {virustotal,abuseipdb,otx,malwarebazaar} [{virustotal,abuseipdb,otx,malwarebazaar} ...]` | Select which threat intel providers to use (default: all configured) |  |
| `--ti-offline` | Use only cached threat intel results (no API calls) |  |
| `--siem-format {cef,syslog,stix,leef,ecs}` | Output scan results in SIEM format |  |
| `--siem-output {file,syslog,http,stdout}` | Where to send SIEM output (default: stdout) | `stdout` |
| `--siem-target TARGET` | Target: file path, host:port for syslog, or URL for http |  |
| `--siem-min-severity SCORE` | Minimum threat score (0-100) to forward to SIEM (default: 0) | `0` |
| `--analytics` | Show scan analytics summary after scanning |  |
| `--analytics-period PERIOD` | Analytics period: 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d (default: 7d) | `7d` |
| `--analytics-export FILE` | Export analytics as CSV to specified file |  |
| `--plugins-dir PLUGINS_DIR` | Directory containing detection plugins (default: plugins/) | `plugins` |
| `--disable-plugins` | Skip loading detection plugins |  |

## `hades forensics`

Surface what a file reveals about its origin and owner: GPS location, camera make/model/serial, lens, software and edit history, authorship, timestamps, and embedded thumbnail.

```
hades forensics [-h] [--format {text,json}] [-o FILE] [--all-tags] [--extract-thumbnail OUT.jpg] [--exiftool-path EXIFTOOL_PATH] [-q] file
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `file` | File to extract metadata forensics from |  |
| `--format {text,json}` | Output format (default: text) | `text` |
| `-o FILE, --output FILE` | Write output to file |  |
| `--all-tags` | Include the full raw tag dump (every extracted metadata field) |  |
| `--extract-thumbnail OUT.jpg` | Write the embedded thumbnail/preview to a file (reveals the original framing of a cropped/redacted image) |  |
| `--exiftool-path EXIFTOOL_PATH` | Path to the exiftool binary (default: 'exiftool' on PATH). When absent, HADES falls back to native Pillow/exifread extraction. | `exiftool` |
| `-q, --quiet` | Minimal output |  |

## `hades monitor`

Start a file monitor that watches one or more directories and automatically scans files as they appear or change.

```
hades monitor [-h] [--webhook WEBHOOK] [--alert-threshold ALERT_THRESHOLD] [--siem-format {cef,syslog,stix,leef,ecs}] [--siem-output {file,syslog,http,stdout}] [--siem-target TARGET] [--zeek-watch DIR] [--suricata-watch DIR] [--email-gateway] [--smtp-port SMTP_PORT] [--ir-mode] [-v] [-q] DIR [DIR ...]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `DIR` | Directories to watch (can specify multiple) |  |
| `--webhook WEBHOOK` | Webhook URL for alert notifications |  |
| `--alert-threshold ALERT_THRESHOLD` | Minimum threat score (0-100) to trigger an alert (default: 70, the start of the HIGH band) |  |
| `--siem-format {cef,syslog,stix,leef,ecs}` | Forward alerts in SIEM format |  |
| `--siem-output {file,syslog,http,stdout}` | Where to send SIEM output (default: stdout) | `stdout` |
| `--siem-target TARGET` | Target: file path, host:port for syslog, or URL for http |  |
| `--zeek-watch DIR` | Start Zeek connector watching extract_files/ directory |  |
| `--suricata-watch DIR` | Start Suricata connector watching filestore/ directory |  |
| `--email-gateway` | Start email attachment scanning SMTP gateway |  |
| `--smtp-port SMTP_PORT` | SMTP listen port for email gateway (default: 10025) | `10025` |
| `--ir-mode` | Incident-response mode: do not redact PII/PHI in alerts (log file, webhook). Default redacts, as `hades scan` does. |  |
| `-v, --verbose` | Verbose output |  |
| `-q, --quiet` | Quiet mode |  |

## `hades serve`

Launch the FastAPI-based HADES API server with optional distributed workers, metrics, and SIEM auto-forwarding.

```
hades serve [-h] [--port PORT] [--host HOST] [--api-workers API_WORKERS] [--api-key KEY] [--db-backend {sqlite}] [--redis-url URL] [--encrypt] [--generate-encryption-key] [--distributed] [--metrics] [--no-metrics] [--metrics-port METRICS_PORT] [--health-check] [--siem-auto-forward] [--siem-format {cef,syslog,stix,leef,ecs}] [--siem-min-severity SCORE] [--demo-mode] [-v] [-q]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--port PORT` | Port for API server (default: 8666) | `8666` |
| `--host HOST` | Host for API server (default: 127.0.0.1) | `127.0.0.1` |
| `--api-workers API_WORKERS` | Number of Uvicorn worker processes (default: 1) | `1` |
| `--api-key KEY` | API authentication key (also via HADES_API_KEY env var) |  |
| `--db-backend {sqlite}` | Database backend (sqlite, the only supported backend) |  |
| `--redis-url URL` | Redis connection URL |  |
| `--encrypt` | Enable at-rest encryption |  |
| `--generate-encryption-key` | Generate and save a new encryption key, then exit |  |
| `--distributed` | Enable distributed worker pool (requires Redis) |  |
| `--metrics` | Enable Prometheus metrics endpoint |  |
| `--no-metrics` | Disable Prometheus metrics endpoint |  |
| `--metrics-port METRICS_PORT` | Port for metrics (default: same as API at /metrics) |  |
| `--health-check` | Run health check and exit with code 0 (healthy) or 1 (unhealthy) |  |
| `--siem-auto-forward` | Enable automatic SIEM forwarding for all scan results |  |
| `--siem-format {cef,syslog,stix,leef,ecs}` | SIEM output format for auto-forwarding |  |
| `--siem-min-severity SCORE` | Minimum threat score (0-100) to forward to SIEM (default: 0) | `0` |
| `--demo-mode` | Start API server in demo mode with rate limiting and restricted features |  |
| `-v, --verbose` | Verbose output |  |
| `-q, --quiet` | Quiet mode |  |

## `hades benchmark`

Execute HADES performance benchmarks to measure scan throughput, latency, memory usage, and scaling characteristics.

```
hades benchmark [-h] [--full | --quick | --scale] [--report] [-o FILE] [--generate-test-corpus N]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--full` | Run full benchmark suite (default) |  |
| `--quick` | Run quick benchmarks only (single-file and small-batch) |  |
| `--scale` | Run scaling-focused benchmarks (directory, concurrent, worker) |  |
| `--report` | Generate Markdown benchmark report |  |
| `-o FILE, --output FILE` | Save benchmark results to file |  |
| `--generate-test-corpus N` | Generate N test files for benchmarking, then exit |  |

## `hades doctor`

Run diagnostic checks on the HADES installation: Python version, ExifTool availability, optional library imports, Docker access, and YARA rule compilation.

```
hades doctor [-h] [--json] [-v] [--ti-live]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output results as JSON instead of a table |  |
| `-v, --verbose` | Show additional detail for each check |  |
| `--ti-live` | Also confirm each configured threat-intel key WORKS by looking up the EICAR test file's hash (network call; off by default for air-gapped hosts) |  |

## `hades sanitize`

Strip metadata using the metascrub engine, verifying removal against the output bytes. The input file is never modified unless --in-place is given.

```
hades sanitize [-h] [-o OUTPUT] [--in-place] [-r] [--remove-all] [--fields FIELDS] [--reset-times] [--dry-run] [--json] [-q] path
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | File or directory to sanitize |  |
| `-o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT` | Output file (single input) or output directory. Default: write alongside the input as <name>.sanitized<ext> |  |
| `--in-place` | Overwrite the input file. The original is NOT recoverable. |  |
| `-r, --recursive` | Recurse into subdirectories when the path is a directory |  |
| `--remove-all` | Remove every metadata field the engine can address |  |
| `--fields FIELDS` | Comma-separated list of specific fields to remove |  |
| `--reset-times` | Also reset the output's filesystem timestamps to the Unix epoch. File times are identifiers in their own right and survive metadata removal. Without this the output carries the time it was written, which is not the original's time but is still a time. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Report what would be done, and whether each format is supported |  |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON instead of a table |  |
| `-q, --quiet` | Suppress per-file output; print only the summary |  |

|---|---|---|
| `--skip-verify` | Skip SHA256 hash verification (not recommended) |  |
| `--allow-downgrade` | Allow installing an older version |  |

## `hades licenses`

Print the third-party NOTICE that ships with HADES, and the full license text of any bundled component.

```
hades licenses [-h] [--list] [--source-offer] [--check] [component]
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `component` | Print the full license text for this component instead of the notice. Available: annotated-doc, annotated-types, anyio, asn1crypto, async-timeout, backports-tarfile, bcrypt, bitstream-vera, boto3, botocore, certifi, certvalidator, cffi, charset-normalizer, click, colorama, configparser, cryptography, et-xmlfile, exceptiongroup, exifread, fastapi, h11, httpcore, httptools, httpx, idna, jmespath, joblib, lxml, metascrub, mscerts, numpy, olefile, openpyxl, orbitron, oscrypto, packaging, pandas, pefile, pi-heif, pikepdf, pillow, psutil, pyarrow, pycparser, pydantic, pydantic-core, pydantic-settings, pyexiftool, pyjwt, python, python-dateutil, python-dotenv, python-multipart, pytz, pyyaml, redis, reportlab, requests, rich, s3transfer, scikit-learn, scipy, setuptools, signify, six, starlette, threadpoolctl, tomli, typing-extensions, typing-inspection, urllib3, uvicorn, uvloop, watchdog, watchfiles, websockets, xgboost, xlsxwriter, yara-python |  |
| `--list` | List bundled third-party components and their licenses |  |
| `--source-offer` | Print DarkHorse's written offer for third-party source code |  |
| `--check` | Verify every bundled attribution file is present and non-empty. Exits 1 if any is missing. Intended for the build guard. |  |

## `hades feedback`

Submit and track false-positive reports. Only the file's SHA-256 is transmitted; the file itself never leaves this machine. Requires a Professional, Team, or Enterprise license.

```
hades feedback [-h] {false-positive,status} ...
```

### `hades feedback false-positive`

Compute the file's SHA-256 locally and submit a false-positive report. The sample is not uploaded. Pass the verdict HADES actually returned for the file with --verdict.

```
hades feedback false-positive [-h] [--explanation EXPLANATION] [--verdict VERDICT] [--evidence EVIDENCE] [--consent-public] [--json] FILE
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `FILE` | Path to the file HADES misclassified (hashed locally, never uploaded) |  |
| `--explanation EXPLANATION, -e EXPLANATION` | Why you believe this is a false positive. 20-4000 characters. |  |
| `--verdict VERDICT` | The verdict HADES returned for this file: CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW / SAFE. Required; HADES does not guess it for you. |  |
| `--evidence EVIDENCE` | Optional reference to supporting evidence already lodged with the portal (max 512 characters). Without it the report is accepted as 'awaiting_evidence' and admin review is blocked until evidence is supplied. |  |
| `--consent-public` | Opt IN to public attribution if the report is approved. Off by default; nothing identifying you is published unless you pass this flag. |  |
| `--json` | Emit the portal response as JSON |  |

### `hades feedback status`

Fetch the current status of one of your own FP reports.

```
hades feedback status [-h] [--json] REPORT_ID
```

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `REPORT_ID` | The report id returned when you submitted the report (a UUID) |  |
| `--json` | Emit the portal response as JSON |  |

## Common Workflows

### Full-spectrum Scan

```bash
hades scan -r -v \
  --ml-detect --threat-intel --behavioral --mitre-map \
  --format json --output full_report.json \
  /evidence/
```

### CI/CD Pipeline Gate

```bash
hades scan -r --fail-on high --format json --output hades-report.json ./artifacts/
```

The exit code is the gate: 0 when every file was scanned and none is at or above the `--fail-on` level, 1 when one is, 2 on a usage or tool error, and 3 when nothing reached the level but some files were not scanned. Treat 3 as a failure in CI unless you have decided otherwise.

### Continuous Monitoring with SIEM

```bash
hades monitor /evidence/incoming \
  --alert-threshold 5 \
  --siem-format cef --siem-output syslog --siem-target siem.corp:514 \
  --webhook https://hooks.slack.com/services/XXX
```

### Forensic Investigation

```bash
# Create a case
hades case create IR-2026-0042

# Scan evidence into the case (use the case ID that `hades case create` printed)
hades scan --case-id IR_UUID -r --ml-detect --threat-intel /evidence/

# Verify chain of custody
hades case verify

# Export evidence package
hades case export IR_UUID
```
